about: A workflow every seller's account can run on a schedule: find every checkout paid since the last run (payment links included), check each amount against the offer, keep one customer record per buyer, send each new buyer the setup email once, and mark a customer ended when their subscription ends. The seller's own Stripe key, offers, email sender and email words are inputs and held values; nothing here names a product or a price. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks).

payload.label: Give paid buyers access
payload.job: Every time it runs (every 15 minutes is the intended schedule), turn each newly paid Stripe checkout into a customer: list the checkouts completed since the last one kept, skip any already kept, check each paid amount against a price the offer declares (a trial checkout is checked by its subscription's amount), keep a customer record keyed by the checkout, send the setup email once with an idempotency key, and mark each customer whose subscription ended as ended, keeping their record. A checkout whose amount matches no declared price is not kept; the seller is told instead. Nothing is charged, refunded or cancelled here.

source.name: tools/take-payments (list completed checkouts, look up a checkout, check what a buyer paid, list ended subscriptions), tools/send-messages (send one email), the account's records door (records:write) and tools/tell-the-person
source.note: Made for selling through a Stripe Payment Link while no hosted app receives Stripe's webhooks: the follow-up reads Stripe instead of waiting for it. It runs on the engine's wake (a repeat every 15 minutes, starting at the first step) once wakes run recipe rows, and by hand through tools:run until then. NOT ADOPTED, with the reason: (1) granting anything from the buyer's browser landing on a success page, because a redirect can be forged; only what Stripe says counts; (2) deleting a customer's record when they cancel, because their records stay theirs; the record is marked ended; (3) sending the setup email from the seller's own mailbox without a sender they set up, so the sender and its held key are inputs.

offer_id.description: The offer whose buyers get access, as named in the checkout's metadata

start_unix.description: Where the first run looks from, in seconds, when no customer record exists yet

customer_record_type.description: The record type each buyer is kept as

email_tool.description: The send-messages tool the seller has a sender and key for

from.description: The address the setup email comes from

text.description: The setup email's words; {email} and {people} are filled per buyer

setup_email.description: The setup email the seller wrote

steps.title: Find where the last run stopped
steps.do: Read the account's records of type input.customer_record_type through the records door. created_after_unix is the largest checkout_created among them, or input.start_unix when there are none. Keep the set of their provider_session_id values and the largest ended_at among records marked ended (ended_after_unix; input.start_unix when there is none).

steps.title: List the checkouts paid since then
steps.do: Call tool:list-completed-stripe-checkouts with { created_after_unix: steps.where-to-start.created_after_unix, offer_id: input.offer_id }. While complete is false, call it again with created_after_unix: next_created_after_unix. Drop every checkout whose provider_session_id is already a customer record: the same checkout can come back in two reads.

steps.title: Check each paid amount against the offer
steps.do: For each new checkout: when amount_total_cents is above 0 it is the paid amount; when it is 0 (a trial), call tool:look-up-a-stripe-checkout with { provider_session_id } and use its recurring_amount_cents. Call tool:check-what-a-buyer-paid with { offer_id: input.offer_id, paid: { amountCents, currency } }. A checkout that does not match, or has no buyer email, is not kept: tell the seller with tool:tell-the-person, naming the checkout id and the reason. people is the paid amount divided by the offer's price per person, when the offer declares one.

steps.title: Keep one customer record per matched checkout
steps.do: For each matched checkout, write one record through the records door (records:write) with type input.customer_record_type and id customer:<provider_session_id>, value { email, offer_id, price_option_id, paid_cents, currency, people, subscription_id, provider_session_id, checkout_created, status: active }. Writing the same id again changes nothing, so a repeated run keeps one record.

steps.title: Send each new customer the setup email once
steps.do: For each record kept in this run whose setup_sent_at is empty, call input.email_tool with { to: email, from: input.from, subject: input.setup_email.subject, text: input.setup_email.text with {email} and {people} filled, idempotencyKey: setup:<provider_session_id> }. Then write setup_sent_at (the send's time) on the record.

steps.title: Mark customers whose subscription ended
steps.do: Call tool:list-ended-stripe-subscriptions with { ended_after_unix: steps.where-to-start.ended_after_unix }. For each ended subscription that is the subscription_id of an active customer record, write status: ended and ended_at on that record. The record is kept: the customer's own records stay theirs, and buying again makes a new active record.
